analysis.title: AppLovin Corp. (APP) Q3'26 Earnings Review: Returning to Strong Revenue Outperformance; Focus Remains on Execution Against Strategic Growth Opportunities
key_insights: GS maintains Neutral on APP and raises its 12-month price target to $445 from $400, implying 63.8% upside to the $271.75 price (as of the 4 Nov 2026 close).
Q3'26 total revenue was $2,185mm vs GS $2,068mm, consensus $2,073mm and guidance of $2.055-2.085bn, a 5.4% beat vs consensus and +55.5% YoY.
Management cited core gaming growth of nearly 50% YoY and Consumer total spend up triple digits % YoY, with positive trends into the Q4 holiday season.
Management described new model improvements and architectures showing early signs of performance gains, and is investing in datacenter hosting costs to support them.
Q3 Adj. EBITDA was $1,842mm vs GS $1,719mm and consensus $1,730mm, with margin of 84.3%. GAAP EPS was $4.30 vs GS $4.01 and consensus $4.03.
Q3 buybacks were ~$1.3bn (~$2.8bn YTD), and the repurchase authorization was increased.
Negatives GS flags: total non-GAAP expenses grew notably QoQ on datacenter hosting and customer acquisition investment, and Q4 revenue guidance implies a modest sequential decel at the midpoint.
GS wants more visibility into the sustainability of growth after more volatile quarterly performance in recent periods, against management's outlook for 30%+ topline growth.
GS says its medium-term estimates could prove conservative, but it will rely on industry channel checks deeper into the quarter before underwriting sustained outperformance.

Estimate changes: Q4'26 revenue $2.39bn (from $2.20bn), Adj. EBITDA $2.02bn (from $1.76bn), GAAP EPS $4.69 (from $4.15). 2027 revenue $10.41bn (from $9.92bn), Adj. EBITDA $8.73bn (from $8.17bn), GAAP EPS $20.79 (from $19.71).
The shares are down 35.3% over 3 months, 42.8% over 6 months and 55.4% over 12 months in absolute terms, per the price performance table.

The PT is an equal blend of 14.5x EV/GAAP EBITDA on NTM+1 year estimates and a modified DCF using 15.0x EV/FCF-SBC on NTM+4 years estimates, discounted back 3 years at 12%. GS scenario values are $210 downside, $445 base and $615 upside.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Neutral and raises the PT from $400 to $445 after Q3'26 beat the Street and Q4 guidance came in above prior expectations. It wants more evidence that growth is sustainable.

sector_views.rationale: GS is constructive long term on above-average advertising growth and a strong margin profile, citing a positive secular growth backdrop for mobile gaming advertising.

earnings_insights: Q3'26 reported (released 11/4 after close, per the 5 Nov report): revenue $2,185mm vs GS est $2,068mm and consensus $2,073mm, guide $2.055-2.085bn, +55.5% YoY.
Q3'26 Adj. EBITDA reported $1,842mm (84.3% margin) vs GS est $1,719mm and consensus $1,730mm, guide $1.71-1.74bn.
Q3'26 GAAP EPS reported $4.30 vs GS est $4.01 and consensus $4.03.
Q3'26 GAAP gross profit reported $1,944mm (89.0% margin) vs GS est $1,815mm and consensus $1,825mm.
Q4'26 company guidance: revenue $2.365-2.395bn and Adj. EBITDA $1.995-2.025bn. GS new estimates are revenue $2,390mm, Adj. EBITDA $2,015mm and GAAP EPS $4.69 (old $4.15), all GS forecasts.

GS FY2026E forecasts: revenue $8,341mm (old $8,033mm), Adj. EBITDA $7,028mm, GAAP EPS $16.29 (old $15.47). FY2027E: revenue $10,414mm, Adj. EBITDA $8,728mm, GAAP EPS $20.79. FY2028E: revenue $12,715mm, Adj. EBITDA $10,634mm, GAAP EPS $26.32.
risk_factors: Data privacy and regulation could impact the effectiveness of APP's ad tech platform and topline growth.
Technical requirements and policies of third-party app distribution channels could impact the growth outlook.
Changes in the competitive environment could impact management's ability to execute.

tension_points.bear_case: Quarterly performance has been volatile in recent periods, Q4 guidance implies a modest sequential decel at the midpoint, and non-GAAP expenses grew notably QoQ on datacenter hosting and customer acquisition.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS looks to its industry channel check work deeper into the quarter before underwriting improved or sustained outperformance.
